title: QBR preflight rehearsal and risk lighthouse
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc is a reusable preflight and rehearsal runbook for quarterly business reviews (QBRs). Focus: reduce surprises, align senior stakeholders, and surface risk early so the meeting stays decision-oriented. Designed for mid-market to strategic accounts where renewals and product adoption are on the line.

Who should use this: CS lead (owner), account executive (optional), product/solutions engineer (technical backup), and the customer success manager (facilitator).

High-level objectives for the QBR meeting (pick 2–3 primary):
- Confirm roadmap alignment and measurable adoption goals for next 90 days.
- Secure renewal signal or explicit next-step commitments.
- Resolve at least one technical or process blocker that’s preventing wider usage.

Preflight checklist (7–10 days out, 72 hours, and 24 hours):
- 7–10 days out:
  - Confirm meeting date/time and attendee roster including exec sponsor. Flag any proxies.
  - Request pre-reads: usage dashboard, support digest, 3 customer success stories, open issues list.
  - Create a 1-slide VOICE-OF-CUSTOMER snapshot (top asks, pain, wins).
  - Draft desired outcomes and decision asks; share with AE for alignment.
  - Book a 30m dry-run with internal core team (CS lead, AE, engineer).
- 72 hours out:
  - Finalize slides and pre-read; send to attendees with 48h expectation.
  - Confirm facilitator and timekeeper. Confirm slide order and expected owner for each slide.
  - Prepare an evidence log with data links (dashboard slices, logs, evals).
- 24 hours out:
  - Run a 20–30m rapid rehearsal (speedrun) of script and transitions.
  - Confirm escalation contacts (names + preferred channel) and a fallback model variant to suggest if performance issues come up.
  - Print or prepare facilitator cue cards (one-liners for each transition).

Roles and responsibilities during rehearsal and meeting:
- Facilitator (CS lead): owns agenda flow, calls decisions and next steps, keeps time.
- Presenter (AE/CSM): owns account context, commercial asks, and follow-up commitments.
- Technical backup (Solutions Eng): stays muted unless called, ready to share screen for quick demo or triage.
- Timekeeper/Notetaker: logs decisions + action owners live into meeting notes doc.

90-minute QBR agenda (template) with facilitation prompts and timing:
- 0:00–0:05 — Welcome & desired outcome (Facilitator)
  Script: "Thanks all — our goal is to leave with clear next steps on adoption and one decision on renewal readiness. If anything is missing, tell me now so we can adjust."
- 0:05–0:15 — Customer highlights & voice-of-customer snapshot (Customer or CSM)
  Prompt: "Share two wins and one open gap. We will reference these in the roadmap alignment segment."
- 0:15–0:30 — Usage + health signal walkthrough (CS lead)
  Evidence: key dashboards, top 3 metrics vs. target. Keep metrics to 3 top-line numbers.
- 0:30–0:45 — Risk Lighthouse — prioritized risks & mitigation lanes (Facilitator)
  Script: "We catalog risks by impact x immediacy. For each risk we recommend an owner and a proposed mitigation within 30 days."
- 0:45–1:05 — Roadmap alignment & feature ask triage (Product/CS)
  Facilitation cue: "We’ll map each ask to an action: plan, backlog, or partner-led solution within 60–90 days."
- 1:05–1:20 — Commercial posture and renewal conversation (AE + Exec Sponsor)
  Cue: use decision language: approve, postpone with date, or escalate to procurement.
- 1:20–1:30 — Decisions, owners, and immediate next steps (Facilitator + Notetaker)
  Close: read out decisions and confirm owners and dates.

Facilitator cue card examples (one-liners to keep flow tight):
- Opening: "Our north star today is X; if we can agree on Y, we’ll have a clear path forward."
- Redirecting a tangent: "Great point — to keep us on time, can we park that in the backlog and schedule a deep dive?"
- When a decision is unclear: "It sounds like we need a follow-up decision: who should own the follow-up and by when?"
- When a blocker appears technical: "Liam, will you own a 72-hour triage and report back with a fix plan?"

Rehearsal runbook (20–30 minute speedrun recommended):
- Start with slide deck open and run entire meeting in real time. Time each segment.
- Practice hand-offs: note who mutes/unmutes, who shares screen.
- Practice two failure modes: the demo fails; the exec sponsor is late. Rehearse fallback lines and who speaks.
- Validate evidence links (no broken dashboards/permissions).
- Confirm that the Notetaker has a template for actions and decision log.

Risk Lighthouse (unique framing):
- Purpose: a concise table in meeting slides that lists the top 4–6 risks, rank-ordered by expected impact on renewal or adoption in the next 90 days. For each risk include: short title, why it matters, immediate mitigation, owner, and SLO for mitigation (date or metric).
- Example lighthouse entries (verbatim language to adapt):
  1) "Integration throughput gap" — Why: throttling observed during peak jobs; Impact: will block X use case; Mitigation: enable batching + config tweak; Owner: Solutions Eng; SLO: reduce 95th percentile latency by 40% within 14 days.
  2) "Feature parity gap for X workflow" — Why: customer cannot migrate a key job; Mitigation: scoped backlog item + partner script; Owner: Product Manager; SLO: ship roadmap spike/update in next 45 days.
  3) "Contract sign-off drift" — Why: procurement needs updated SLAs; Mitigation: AE to secure meeting with legal; Owner: AE; SLO: procurement meeting scheduled within 10 business days.

Escalation lanes (Speedrun escalation lanes):
- Tier 1 — internal rapid triage (CS lead + SE): channel: #cs-qbr-triage (Slack), phone: SE on-call. Response SLA: 4 business hours.
- Tier 2 — engineering & infra engagement: open a JIRA incident, tag eng-sre lead. Response SLA: 24 hours for mitigation plan.
- Tier 3 — executive escalations for contractual/SLAs: escalate to VP CS and legal with a decision brief. Response SLA: 48 hours.

Post-meeting actions and follow-up template (to send within 24 hours):
- Subject line: "[Company] QBR — Decisions & 30/60/90 Day Plan"
- Body: 1–2 line recap of outcome, explicit decisions and owners (table), 30/60/90 day milestones with owners, next checkpoint date, link to meeting notes and recording, ask for any missing invitees to confirm availability.
- Attach: action tracker (shared sheet), updated risk lighthouse snapshot, slide deck PDF.

Success metrics to measure QBR effectiveness (quarterly):
- % of QBRs with a recorded decision (target > 90%).
- % of risks with mitigation progress within SLA (target > 80%).
- Renewal signal change rate within 30 days of QBR (net positive delta in renewal probability).
- Customer satisfaction with QBR (post-meeting 3-question pulse NPS).

Appendix: quick scripts for common tense moments
- Exec sponsor is late: "We’ll start with the highlights and save the commercial discussion for when [exec] joins — if they don’t make it, we’ll capture a decision window and circulate."
- Demo fails: "Thanks — we have a playback screenshot and logs; Liam will triage and follow up with a fix plan within 72 hours. For now, here’s the short demo recording that shows the expected behavior."
- Procurement pushes back on SLA: "We can outline option A (standard SLA) and option B (SLA + indemnity addendum). Let’s capture your priority and have our legal partner follow up within 10 business days."

Checklist quick-reference (one page to hand to facilitator):
- Confirmed attendees + exec sponsor
- Pre-read sent with 48h lead time
- Evidence links validated
- Rehearsal completed within 24h
- Escalation contacts confirmed
- Notetaker template ready
- Risk Lighthouse slide prepared and prioritized

Notes and provenance:
- This doc is a synthesis of recurring practices observed across strategic accounts and an evolving internal QBR framework. Use freely and adapt language to customer tone.
- Last major revision: Feb 2026 rehearsal flow update and added risk lighthouse examples.

Related artifacts and where to store final artifacts after meeting:
- Slide deck (final PDF) -> Confluence page and account folder in Drive.
- Action tracker -> shared customer success sheet (link in meeting notes).
- Decision log -> append to account playbook page in Confluence.

End of document.
